description: F-CORE-045: an account may be posted to only inside its validity window. THE FINDING BEHIND THIS FIXTURE is not a wrong number but a silent one — `validFrom` and `validTo` were declared on `account` in the normative format schema and no implementation read or wrote them; `importChartOfAccounts` dropped them without a word, so an account carrying `validTo: 2025-12-31` accepted a posting dated 2026-06-01 exactly as if the field had never been there. A field the schema declares and the engine ignores is the mirror image of the rule the project already has for the other direction, and it is worse in one respect: whoever set it believed it did something. WHY THIS IS NOT A LOCK, and why both have to exist: `E_ACCOUNT_LOCKED` is unconditional and about NOW — it refuses every posting, including a late correction dated before the lock, which is precisely wrong for an account retired at a year end. The window is judged against the POSTING's date, so 1901 keeps taking its December correction (step 4) and refuses January (step 3). A caller that could not tell the two refusals apart could not tell a user whether to unlock the account or fix the date. WRITES ONLY: the trial balance at the end still carries every account outside its window with every figure ever posted to it, because the history happened — a window that hid past figures would make the books say less than the journal does. The last step proves the guard on the master data itself: a window that closes before it opens accepts nothing at all, so the account would be created dead and every later refusal would name a date rather than the cause.

expect.comment: Inside the window, so nothing fires. An account with a window behaves exactly like one without for every date it covers.

Balanced, vouchered, in an open period, on an account that exists and is not locked — and refused, because the account was retired at the year end. Before this the posting went through and the account carried a 2027 balance nobody had planned for.

THE DIFFERENCE FROM A LOCK, in one step: the same account that just refused January takes December, because the window is judged against the posting's own date. A lock would have refused this too, which is why retiring an account was not expressible before.

input.text: Konto, das es 2026 noch nicht gibt

expect.comment: The other edge of the window. A chart position introduced for the coming year must not quietly collect this year's postings.

input.name: Fenster, das vor seinem Anfang schliesst

expect.comment: Refused at the master data, not at the first posting. An account with an empty window accepts nothing at all, and every refusal it produced later would have named a date instead of the reason.
Both bounds absent is what every account had before the window existed and what almost every account keeps. Nothing changes for it.
The window is readable — a screen offering an account picker must be able to grey out what the date does not allow, instead of letting the user post and then translating an error code.
1901 is outside its window from 2027 on and still carries everything ever posted to it. The window governs writes and never reads.
The window has no effect on a carry-forward either: 1900 crosses into 2027 with its opening balance while 1901, whose window ended, simply has nothing left to carry.
